source_metadata.title: Intensive versus Conventional Glucose Control in Critically Ill Patients

atoms.canonical_statement: NICE-SUGAR tested whether intensive glucose control reduces all-cause mortality at 90 days in critically ill adults.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We designed the ... NICE-SUGAR trial to test the hypothesis that intensive glucose control reduces mortality at 90 days.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study was a parallel-group randomized controlled trial conducted in 42 ICUs (38 academic tertiary-care and 4 community hospitals).

population.label: Adults admitted to participating ICUs and randomized in NICE-SUGAR

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients assigned to intensive glucose control had a target blood glucose range of 81-108 mg/dL (4.5-6.0 mmol/L), managed with intravenous insulin using a computerized algorithm.

exposures.details: Target blood glucose 81-108 mg/dL (4.5-6.0 mmol/L) using intravenous insulin guided by a computerized algorithm.

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients assigned to conventional glucose control had a target blood glucose of 180 mg/dL or less; insulin was started above 180 mg/dL and reduced then stopped below 144 mg/dL.

exposures.details: Target blood glucose <=180 mg/dL (<=10.0 mmol/L); insulin initiated above 180 mg/dL and reduced/discontinued below 144 mg/dL.

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary outcome was death from any cause within 90 days after randomization.

outcome.definition: Death from any cause within 90 days after randomization.

atoms.canonical_statement: Of 6104 randomized patients, 3054 were assigned to intensive control and 3050 to conventional control; primary-outcome data were available for 3010 and 3012 patients, respectively.

atoms.canonical_statement: Baseline characteristics were similar between groups; mean age was about 60 years, approximately 63% were male, mean APACHE II score was 21.1, and about 37% were operative admissions.

atoms.canonical_statement: Time-weighted blood glucose from randomization to cessation of study treatment averaged 115 mg/dL with intensive control and 144 mg/dL with conventional control (difference -29 mg/dL, 95% CI -30 to -28; P<0.001).

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligibility depended partly on the subjective expectation that the patient would require a prolonged ICU stay.
Treating staff and study personnel could not be blinded to treatment-group assignment.
A substantial proportion of intensive-control patients achieved glucose levels modestly above the assigned target range.
The trial did not collect specific data to determine the biological mechanisms of the interventions or their costs.
The investigators concluded that targeting blood glucose below 180 mg/dL resulted in lower mortality than targeting 81-108 mg/dL and did not recommend the lower target for critically ill adults.
